title: Finish what the pane host left: stale session socket, editor, orphans
notes: The pane host (panes-decision-1) keeps worker shells across a restart. Left for this card: (1) a kept shell's DASHBOARD_SOCKET names the dead run's session socket, so `dashboard pane …` from a kept pane says the app quit; give the session socket a stable path in user data. (2) The editor runs in the app and starts fresh after a restart, because nvim's socket is named after the pid and slot (nvim-remote.ts); name it by pane key and keep it in the host like any pane. (3) Kept shells of a project not reopened run unseen; offer them or kill them once the restore is done. (4) A protocol-version change orphans the old host's shells. (5) Efficiency: every byte is parsed by two headless xterms (host and app), the survivors' screens sit in main until adopted, and data goes one JSON line per pty read. (6) workflow-rule-1 can be relaxed once 1 and the Claude screens' restart cost are settled. See docs/panes/README.md Open questions.
